cands.name: Toni Kornegay Vaughn

top: Shelby County Democratic Party Executive Committee
money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Retired insurance claims executive who rose to Senior Regional Vice President for the southeastern U.S. at a national independent adjusting company, overseeing 40 branch offices. University of Alabama finance graduate (1975). Democratic nominee for Alabama House District 45 in 2026. Has not held public office.

endorsements.text: In her Ballotpedia survey she lists endorsements from the Alabama AFL-CIO, Central Alabama Labor Council, Gun Sense Candidate, Mental Health Candidate, the Alabama Democratic County Chairs Association, and the Shelby, Jefferson and St. Clair County Democratic parties (self-reported).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Vaughn was born or which county she grew up in. She has held no public office, so there is no record of official actions. We found no stated positions on data centers, development and growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land purchases, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, or abortion. Her campaign site covers education, affordability, childcare and healthcare in general terms only. Her endorsement list comes from her own survey answers; we did not confirm it with the endorsing groups.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Said in her Ballotpedia survey that her education priorities include repealing the CHOOSE Act (Alabama's school-choice program) and protecting public school funding; she also said she supports teachers.

clean-money.evidence: Said in her Ballotpedia survey, "I am committed to the people, not mega donors or outside interests." This is a general statement, not a specific pledge to refuse any category of contribution.

cands.name: Susan DuBose

top: Alapac Alabama Medical PAC State Fund
money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican state representative for Alabama House District 45 since November 2022. Retired commercial banker (Compass Bank) with a finance degree from the University of South Alabama and an MBA from Spring Hill College. Former president of Republican Women of North Shelby County.
cands.gaps: We found no documented votes or sponsored bills we could read, so there is no record of what she did on the issues listed here. We found nothing from her on data centers, development or growth, foreign ownership of land, H-1B visas, immigration enforcement or homestead property taxes. Her site pledges no new taxes and a lower grocery tax, but does not address homestead taxes specifically. Her 2022 survey answers are the only detailed interview-style statements found; she did not complete the 2026 Ballotpedia survey. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for 2026, and no controversies appeared in the pages we had.

local.label: Roots 55: She was born in Biloxi and raised on the Mississippi Gulf Coast, earned her degree in Mobile by 1985, and has lived in Shelby County since 1988, more than 35 years. · Money: 0% of money from District 45 ZIP codes

qual.background: Alabama House member since 2022, re-elected in 2026. Earlier she was a Compass Bank residential, commercial and construction loan officer and business development officer, with a B.S. in finance and an MBA.
qual.why: Nearly four years of legislative service plus a lending and finance career put her in the high range; committee seats were not counted.
qual.label: Nearly four years of legislative service plus a lending and finance career put her in the high range; committee seats were not counted.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her campaign site says families now have school options through the CHOOSE Act and that educational options for families will produce the best results.

second-amendment.evidence: Her campaign site says she will not vote for any measure that limits law-abiding citizens' access to the weapons they choose for protection.

pro-life.evidence: Her campaign site says she is '100% pro-life,' that life begins at conception, and that she will vote to protect unborn babies.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site calls support for law enforcement a top priority and backs stiffer penalties for the worst crimes and an end to bail for repeat violent offenders.

clean-money.evidence: In her 2022 Ballotpedia survey she said unlimited special-interest contributions in Alabama 'need to stop' and listed limiting them as a passion issue.
